# Statement-coverage baseline for the merged unit + acceptance profile.
#
# `tfkit coverage readme` (`make coverage-readme`) renders README.md's badge and
# coverage block from this file, and `tfkit coverage gate` (`make coverage-gate`)
# fails a run whose merged coverage falls below a `floor_*` value. The badge,
# the block and the gate therefore cannot disagree: they all read this file, and
# CI fails when README.md is out of sync with it.
#
# Keys. `measured_<scope>` names a scope and needs a matching `floor_<scope>`;
# `_` is the path separator in the rendered label, so `measured_internal_client`
# renders `internal/client`. `measured_total` is required and drives the badge.
# `measured_commit` and `measured_date` describe the last measurement,
# `target`/`gold` are the tracked milestones.
#
# The gate is `make coverage-gate` (`tfkit coverage gate`), which the `Coverage`
# job runs on every pull request after the acceptance container has written its
# profile. It parses this file with the same rules as `tfkit coverage readme` and
# additionally requires every scope named here to appear in the merged profile:
# a missing, misspelled or stray `floor_*`, or a scope that drops out of the
# profile, is a configuration error (exit 2), never a pass.
#
# The measurement is the merged profile the committed tooling produces: the bare
# unit profile (`make coverage`, `coverage.out`) merged with the instrumented
# acceptance container's profile (`coverage-acceptance.out`,
# `-covermode=atomic -coverpkg=./internal/...`) by `tfkit coverage merge`
# (`make coverage-merge`). To raise the floor: run `make coverage` and
# `make coverage-merge`, update `measured_*` and `floor_*` here, then run
# `make coverage-readme` and commit the result.
#
# `measured_*` is what the project last observed; `floor_*` is the enforced
# minimum, kept half a point below the measurement (rounded down to the next half
# point) so environment jitter cannot fail a run on its own.
#
# The scopes below the four original ones are the areas the coverage issues named
# as real gaps; each floor is only as high as the tests committed with it. A floor
# is never lowered: raising one is a deliberate line in a pull request.
#
# Deliberately not a scope: internal/datasources/secrets. It wraps the Gravitino
# 1.4 secrets API, which cannot be exercised against the 1.1.1–1.3.1 servers this
# provider supports, so a floor there would measure the fake only.

# Last measurement: merged unit + acceptance on Go 1.27.2, 7,661 statements.
measured_internal_client=91.3
measured_internal_models=86.5
measured_internal_provider=95.8
measured_internal_client_auth=76.7
measured_internal_datasources_schema=97.0
measured_internal_datasources_policy=87.1
measured_internal_datasources_role=87.0
measured_internal_datasources_fileset=87.3
measured_internal_datasources_partition=94.0
measured_internal_resources_partition=92.2
measured_total=85.2
measured_commit=d000380
measured_date=2026-11-24

# Enforced floor.
floor_internal_client=90.5
floor_internal_models=86.0
floor_internal_provider=95.0
floor_internal_client_auth=76.0
floor_internal_datasources_schema=96.5
floor_internal_datasources_policy=86.5
floor_internal_datasources_role=86.5
floor_internal_datasources_fileset=86.5
floor_internal_datasources_partition=93.5
floor_internal_resources_partition=91.5
floor_total=84.5

# Milestones tracked in the issue tracker.
target=80
gold=90
